Existing Python AntiSkillSubjectV1 decoder recomputes the semantic ID and Unicode normalization; this native host validates closed raw JSON/types and binds its exact bytes, then checks supplied semantic ID equals the raw subject field. Native alone does not independently recompute the semantic ID.

Live scope coverage is only candidate_patch, candidate_result and adversary_bout_dispatch, across the four declared stages. Uncovered scope never yields CLEAR; hits may impose a stronger refusal.
Six historical fixtures are private predicate replay controls; their original unrestricted scopes are not relabelled as live profile acceptance.
Inner subject JSON is bounded to 32KiB; the existing executable also bounds the whole runtime request to 64KiB. Escaping overhead may refuse a request before inner evaluation.

Every decision binds task, stage, existing semantic identity, exact raw subject hash and all three compiled pins. Exactly one task tag and one valid request digest tag are required; the caller adapter separately binds that request digest to the actual request.
Named sorted UTF8 compact JSON profile core.native.antiskill.json.v1 is used for hashes; no RFC8785 claim.

Native decisions have authority_effect None and can_authorize false. Provider execution, model verification, human admission, full cross-engine routing and general mathematical claims are outside these native controls.
Parent owns Python adapter/composition evidence. This native handoff does not claim that their final integration tests passed.
